title: group Module
content_markdown: This module provides functionalities for different methods of group membership checking.
overview: This module provides functionalities for different methods of group membership checking.
how_it_works:
Strict membership checking: There is a database table that contains list of users and groups they belong to. The module provides the possibility to check if a specific user belongs to a specific group. There is no DB caching support, each check involving a DB query.

Regular Expression based checking: Another database table contains list of regular expressions and group IDs. A matching occurs if the user URI match the regular expression. This type of matching may be used to fetch the group ID(s) the user belongs to (via RE matching) . Due performance reasons (regular expression evaluation), DB cache support is available: the table content is loaded into memory at startup and all regular expressions are compiled.

exported_parameters.description: URL of the database table to be used.

exported_parameters.name: table
exported_parameters.description: Name of the table holding strict definitions of groups and their members.

exported_parameters.name: user_column
exported_parameters.description: Name of the “table” column holding usernames.

exported_parameters.name: domain_column
exported_parameters.description: Name of the “table” column holding domains.

exported_parameters.name: group_column
exported_parameters.description: Name of the “table” column holding groups.

exported_parameters.name: use_domain
exported_parameters.description: If enabled (set to non zero value) then domain will be used also used for strict group matching; otherwise only the username part will be used.

exported_parameters.name: re_table
exported_parameters.description: Name of the table holding definitions for regular-expression based groups. If no table is defined, the regular-expression support is disabled.

exported_parameters.name: re_exp_column
exported_parameters.description: Name of the “re\_table” column holding the regular expression used for user matching.

exported_parameters.name: re_gid_column
exported_parameters.description: Name of the “re\_table” column holding the group IDs.

exported_parameters.name: multiple_gid
exported_parameters.description: If enabled (non zero value) the regular-expression matching will return all group IDs that match the user; otherwise only the first will be returned.

exported_parameters.name: aaa_url
exported_parameters.description: This is the url representing the AAA protocol used and the location of the configuration file of this protocol.

exported_functions.name: db_is_user_in

parameters.name: uri
parameters.description: a SIP URI whose username and optionally domain to be used.
valid_values: (default) - parse the given input as a SIP URI

return_values.condition: username in the given URI is member of the given group
username in the given URI is not member of the given group

exported_functions.description: This function is to be used for script group membership. The function returns true if username in the given URI is member of the given group and false if not.

exported_functions.name: db_get_user_group

parameters.name: uri
parameters.description: a SIP URI to be matched against the regular expressions
valid_values: (default) - parse the given input as a SIP URI

parameters.name: output_avp
parameters.description: a list of matched group IDs

return_values.condition: the username in the given uri belongs to at least one group

exported_functions.description:
This function is to be used for regular expression based group membership, using DB support. The function returns true if the username in the given "uri" belongs to at least one group.

All matching group IDs shall be returned in "output_avp" if multiple_gid is enabled, otherwise only the first one to match (the records are attempted in reversed order of the results returned by the RDBMS).
